**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment or take-or-pay exposure on IBM:

- **§ 6.0** — we agree to purchase Products only subject to the Agreement, and it "does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product" absent orders.
- **§ 6.1** — we may cancel any and all Purchase Orders at any time, with no cancellation charge where MSL is in default.
- **§ 13.0(a)/(f)** — MSL owns and is liable for inventory; we bear no carrying, warehousing, excess or scrap costs.
- **§ 13.2(e)** — "IBM will have no liability for unused flexibility," so the Appendix 4 volume-flexibility band is a supplier-side commitment to us, not a commitment by us.
- **§ 13.3(b)** — EOL inventory not transferred remains MSL's sole responsibility.

The only volume-linked payment is the Appendix 2 requirements-accuracy compensation (percentage of material cost if our forecast accuracy drops below the stated threshold). That functions as a forecast true-up for material MSL procured against our forecast — not a shortfall penalty or multi-year commitment — so it sits within the playbook's accepted structure. I noted in the finding that this true-up carries no aggregate cap, which is worth raising only if the pricing appendices are otherwise reopened.
